# `.github/workflows/`

**The GitHub Actions workflows: the slowest tier of the gate ladder, the pull-request reviewer,
whose approval GitHub's auto-merge waits for, and the nightly prompt review.** Each file's header is the authority on it. Where a
row here and a header disagree, the header wins and the row is corrected.

| File | What it is, or what it refuses |
|---|---|
| `verify.yml` | Every gate that reads only committed files, cheapest first. It runs on every pull request and every push to `main`, the push an auto-merge makes among them, and by hand. It trusts none of the faster tiers (`CLAUDE.md` § The gate ladder). Each job that runs a gate checks out the whole history, which `trace:check` walks, installs the toolchain `mise.toml` pins through `jdx/mise-action`, locked (`docs/decisions.md` § D-31), and runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. Its jobs are split so no pull request's code off the floor runs before a gate the floor holds (`docs/decisions.md` § D-55): `floor-gates` runs the gates that read the product, `product-gates` those that run it, `gates` every other, and `verify`, the check the trunk's ruleset requires, passes only when the three did. `pr-review:check` holds the split. |
| `pr-review.yml` | The pull-request reviewer (`docs/decisions.md` § D-57, amending § D-47). On each head a pull request against `main` is given, `scripts/pr-review.mjs review` submits one review from the high-risk floor alone: off it, an approval, the one the trunk's ruleset requires, and GitHub's auto-merge merges the head once `verify` passes too; on it, a comment that a person decides, and a person approves and merges it. It runs on `pull_request_target`, so the trunk's copy runs, and it reads the head only as git objects. Its one job holds `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write` and nothing else: it merges nothing, sets no status and dispatches nothing. No language model and no secret takes part, and it installs no npm package. It takes from `mise.toml`, through `jdx/mise-action`, only the tools it runs: Node and gh. It reads a token and the network, so it is no tier of the ladder: `pr-review:check` and `pr-review:selftest` hold its wiring and its decisions, at push and in `verify.yml`. |
| `prompt-review.yml` | The prompt review (`docs/decisions/asdlc-openspec-ic9h.md` § Decision), and the home of when a review starts and of its name. It runs nightly on `schedule` while the variable `PROMPT_REVIEW_SCHEDULED` is `true`, and on a person's dispatch, and on no other event. Each of its three jobs runs on a runner of its own and holds `contents: read`. `pending` holds no secret: with the run's own read token it bootstraps the tracker, lists what is pending and counts the open review pull requests. `figures` holds the two Langfuse projects' keys and runs only files on the high-risk floor. `review` mints one token of the agents' App before any code off the floor runs, deletes the key, runs the `continuous-prompt-improvement` agent through `anthropics/claude-code-action` with the Anthropic and TypeSafe keys, and revokes the token at its end. `figures` and `review` name the `prompt-review` environment, which deploys from `main` alone and holds every secret the workflow reads. It reviews only while something is pending and no review pull request is open. A dispatch with `mode: probe` makes one model turn in place of the review, so a person can test each credential first. It reads secrets, the network and a model, so it is no tier of the ladder: `pr-review:check` refuses a read of the App's key in any other workflow, on any other event or outside the environment, and `check:toolchain` holds its mise. |
